99.0.s.en: (1) The greatness of the awesome Lord

99.0.0.en: 1- The LORD reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth between the cherubims; let the earth be moved.

99.0.1.en: 1- When the glory of God appeared in His ministry on earth, that is, in His teachings and miracles, the hearts of many trembled and they repented and believed in Him; and when He was lifted up on the Cross and died to redeem us, the demons who lead the peoples astray through the pagan gods trembled. And at the end of days, when the Lord the King and Judge appears, the unbelieving peoples will tremble, because He will punish them with eternal perdition.

99.0.2.en: 2- The Lord the King sits upon the cherubim, who are the angels full of eyes and knowledge; He is eternal and established and sits upon those who know Him, who are the cherubim, and likewise upon everyone who believes in Him and knows Him and loves Him. And when the demons working on the earth see the King, God, sitting upon the cherubim, who became incarnate and redeemed us on the Cross, their kingdom, which leads astray those on the earth, is shaken.

99.1.0.en: 2- The LORD is great in Zion; and he is high above all the people.

99.1.1.en: 1- God is great in the midst of His people, that is, Zion, throughout the Old Testament; He is known, His works are many, and His miracles are mighty among them. And He is exalted above all peoples, that is, above all the pagan gods that the Gentiles worship, for they are nothing before Him, because those in them are demons. On the other hand, every humble heart enjoys God’s reign over it, but as for the one who is proud, God exalts Himself over him to make him feel his weakness.

99.1.2.en: 2- The Lord is great in His Temple in Jerusalem, and His worship is holy and higher than all the evil pagan worship spread among the Gentiles in their unclean temples and all the defiled lusts connected with it.

99.2.0.en: 3- Let them praise thy great and terrible name; for it is holy.

99.2.1.en: When believers become accustomed to thanking God and praising His holy name, their hearts are moved by love for Him and they feel His greatness, and then their hearts are filled with fear of Him, so they keep away from sins, which encourages them to cling to God and to thank Him and praise Him. Thus praise encourages them to the fear of God, and the fear of God encourages them to praise.

99.2.2.en: Contemplate the holiness of God and His righteousness, so that your heart is lifted up to Him and you cling to Him in prayers and praises and meditations on His word, and then it becomes easy for you to leave your sins and the enticements of evil, and this in turn helps you to lift your heart to God, so that you always grow in His love and always keep your peace.

99.3.0.en: 4- The king’s strength also loveth judgment; thou dost establish equity, thou executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.

99.3.1.en: 1- The King, who is God, has as His glory and greatness that He loves truth and justice, whatever the price of justice. And man’s sin deserved eternal death, so Christ became incarnate and redeemed him, to fulfill divine justice and save man.

99.3.2.en: 2- In God is perfect uprightness, and He showed uprightness in the conscience of man whom He created, and then in the commandments and the Law of Moses. And finally He showed the perfection of uprightness in the Law of the New Testament. So He establishes uprightness forever.

99.3.3.en: 3- God gave an example to the whole world in judgment and justice when He chose His people in the Old Testament, and gave them the commandments and the Law, and judged them by it, so He honored the righteous such as Abraham and David, and punished the wicked such as Achan son of Carmi, and Hophni and Phinehas; indeed, He blessed and rewarded all His people by their possessing the land of Canaan and punished them with captivity.

99.4.0.en: 5- Exalt ye the LORD our God, and worship at his footstool; for he is holy.

99.4.1.en: 1- Believers in God ought to exalt Him in their sight and their prayers above every power in the world, for He is the only God, and they worship at His feet, declaring their submission to Him and to His perfect holiness. This helps them to worship God and receive spiritual enlightenment, so that they know Him and discover His secrets and enjoy Him.

99.4.2.en: 2- “Exalt the Lord” was fulfilled when they lifted Him up on the Cross. And worshiping at His footstool means worshiping in His Temple in Jerusalem, or worshiping in the New Testament at the foot of the Cross, and it is worship in purity and holiness, because He is holy.

99.5.0.en: 6- Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name; they called upon the LORD, and he answered them. 7- He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance that he gave them.

99.5.1.en: 1- The salvation accomplished by the Cross was spoken of by the prophets in the Old Testament, and by well-known men of God such as Moses, Aaron and Samuel. And because Moses, Aaron and Samuel prayed and interceded for the people of God, and the basic function of the priest is to intercede for his people before God, Moses was called a priest, as was Samuel, although they were not priests, but they prayed for the people of God, as Moses prayed for the people when he fought Amalek (Ex 17:8-16) and as Samuel prayed much for his people (1 Sam 7:8, 9).

99.5.2.en: 2- God showed His love and care for His people by the pillar of cloud, from behind which He spoke from inside the tabernacle of meeting, and He cared for them because they held fast to His commandments and submitted to Him.

99.5.3.en: 3- The pillar of cloud symbolizes the Incarnation of Christ, for God was hidden behind the pillar of cloud, and likewise Christ hid His divinity in His body. And Moses, Aaron and Samuel offered animal sacrifices as a symbol of Christ, the true Sacrifice on the Cross.

99.6.0.en: 8- Thou answeredst them, O LORD our God: thou wast a God that forgavest them, though thou tookest vengeance of their deeds.

99.6.1.en: 1- God rejoiced in the prayers of His children Moses, Aaron and Samuel and all the prophets and men of God in the Old Testament. And He answered their prayers and gave care to His people, and took vengeance on their enemies such as Amalek, and those who murmured against the priesthood such as Korah, Dathan and Abiram, and the Philistines, and the enemies of the people of God, who submitted to David the prophet.

99.6.2.en: 2- The Lord’s answer to His devout men was fulfilled in His Incarnation and redemption, and His vengeance on Satan when He bound him on the Cross.

99.7.0.en: 9- Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at his holy hill; for the LORD our God is holy.

99.7.1.en: 1- The psalmist concludes his psalm with the glorification of God the King and worship on His holy mountain, by which he means the places that God sanctified by His dwelling, such as Mount Sinai, and he affirms here the importance of honoring God and submitting to Him in order to receive His salvation.

99.7.2.en: 2- He affirms the importance of the Cross, by which we receive salvation, which was lifted up on the mountain of Golgotha, so when we worship it we declare our submission to His holiness and so receive His salvation.

99.7.3.en: To the extent that you submit to God and His will you give yourself an opportunity to receive God’s blessings and salvation from your sins; indeed, you can intercede for others, caring for the salvation of all.

99.7.4.en: Thanksgiving for God’s mercies: “Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands” v. 1 Introduction:

99.7.5.en: 1- Its author: there are two opinions:

99.7.6.en: a- The author is not mentioned in the title of this psalm, so it is one of the orphan psalms.

99.7.7.en: b- David the prophet, as is stated in the title of this psalm in the Septuagint.

99.7.8.en: 2- This psalm is liturgical; that is, the people sang it with the chorus of the Levites to praise God and thank Him. It was sung during the offering of worship in the Temple of God, especially at the offering of peace offerings, that they might thank God.

99.7.9.en: 3- The purpose of this psalm is to declare that joy moves man to worship God and thank Him, just as praise generates joy within man.

99.7.10.en: 4- This psalm is considered one of the messianic psalms, since it calls the whole earth, and not only the Jews, to praise God, because Christ offered salvation to the whole world.

99.7.11.en: 5- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Agpeya among the psalms of the Ninth Hour, in which Christ completed redemption by His death on the Cross; therefore the believers in God thank Him and praise Him for the salvation offered to them.

100.0.0.en: 1- Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.

100.0.1.en: 1- David the prophet, in the spirit of prophecy, calls all the inhabitants of the earth, not only to believe in God but to thank Him and praise Him in a raised voice, which is the joyful shout, declaring their following of Him, their love, and their joy in their relationship with God.

100.0.2.en: 2- The reason for the joyful shout is the victory of Christ over Satan by the Cross, for He bound him; this psalm, as we said, is messianic and prophesies of the redemption that was accomplished in the fullness of time, by which mankind gained victory over Satan.

100.1.0.en: 2- Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing.

100.1.1.en: 1- Drawing near to God and worshiping Him fills the heart of man with joy, because the best place is the presence of God, and therefore the Church is considered the icon of heaven on earth. So the worship of God gives man joy and delight, and it is a pledge of the glories of the Kingdom of Heaven.

100.1.2.en: 2- Entering into the presence of God is worship in His Temple and His worship, and it is also worshiping God in the Church, and likewise enjoying His presence in the inner room. And before the glory of God and His beauty the heart of man exults and sings, because he has been freed from his sins by repentance and has cast them out before entering into the presence of God. And the sense of God’s presence shines forth in the sacraments of the Church, for God is present in the sacrament of confession and the sacrament of Communion, which man practices often in the New Testament, and he rejoices in the presence of God.

100.1.3.en: 3- True joy is in the worship of the Lord, and not in the joys of the world and its passing lusts, which leave behind sorrow and deprivation, whereas the joyful worship of God gives lasting peace.

100.1.4.en: May you understand the words of prayer so that you speak them with your tongue and your heart, and God will give you joy during worship and make you feel His presence, so that you rise above all your pains.

100.2.s.en: (2) God the Creator and the Faithful

100.2.0.en: 3- Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and we are his; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.

100.2.1.en: 1- Here he speaks of the Lord Jesus Christ and declares that He is God, and that out of His love for His creation He endured sufferings and bore sins in its place in order to redeem it. And no one can offer this infinite love except God alone.

100.2.2.en: 2- If God is our Maker, then our life is His property, and if He is our Shepherd who provides for our needs every day, then we must live for Him and serve Him faithfully and praise Him at all times.

100.3.0.en: 4- Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.

100.3.1.en: David repeats the call to believers in God to worship Him, praise Him and thank Him, and to enter His courts through His gates. And what are the gates?

100.3.2.en: 1- Faith in God and confession of His holy name.

100.3.4.en: 3- The sacrament of Baptism, by which we enter into sonship of the Church.

100.3.5.en: 4- Prayer, which brings us into the presence of God in heaven, and we enjoy meeting Him.

100.3.6.en: 5- The Holy Bible, for it is the door of the great treasure, and we eat and are satisfied from its word and meditate on it.

100.3.7.en: 6- Communion from the Holy Mysteries, which is the door of union with God and abiding in Him. For the courts are not only the porticoes of the Temple in the Old Testament, but are a prophecy of the churches of the New Testament, which are completed in the glories of the heavenly Kingdom.

100.4.0.en: 5- For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.

100.4.1.en: 1- The goodness of God appears in His many kindnesses to His people, not only in the Old Testament but even more in the New Testament, when He died on the Cross for our salvation; therefore praise is due to Him at all times.

100.4.2.en: 2- The second attribute that this verse mentions to us is His mercy, for He loves His children when they fall into sin, and forgives them when they repent, however often their sins are repeated, so there is no God who is merciful to this extent.

100.4.3.en: 3- The third attribute in God is His faithfulness in His promises to His children, and His perfect care for them through the days, that is, “from generation to generation,” and this means His care in the Old Testament and the New Testament, and His care for His children on earth and in heaven. For all this He deserves praise, thanksgiving and glorification continually, because the goodness of God, His mercy and His faithfulness continue, and consequently thanking Him and praising Him lasts forever.

100.4.4.en: Contemplate God’s mercy in your life and how He forgave you all that you did wrong toward Him, and toward His children, mankind, and toward yourself also because you are His child. And thank Him for His forgiveness, and let the divine mercy turn your life into a positive launch in His love, to make up for what you have missed and to enjoy new depths in His love.
